answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each identity to lock a refundable bond in a shared vault before it may trade, with the bond priced so spawning thousands of fakes costs more than they could earn. Reputation then accrues only to identities with a verifiable history of completed work, like layers of karst laid down over time, and newcomers start on a narrow mesa of limited permissions until peer attestations widen their access. An attacker who burns one identity loses both bond and history, so faking scale becomes an expensive climb, not a cheap copy.
